full_judgment:
11. Considering the definition of "worker" before amendment in 2013 (as quoted above), the Legislature has excluded two categories of persons who were holding administrative "প্রশাসনিক” and “managerial" "ব্যবস্থাপনামূলক" post from being called a worker. However, vide the amendment so made in 2013 "তদারকি কর্মকর্তা” "supervisor" has also been included within the ambit of exclusionary clause. 

 13. With the inclusion of the words "কম্পানীর সুবিধাভোগী" the Legislature has included all categories of persons holding any posts whatsoever including managerial, administrative and supervisory in the respective company at least for a period of 9(nine) months, except the owner, partner or members of the management of the company. 

 14. Thus, it can clearly be discerned that person employed by the company before amendment of the Act, 2006 holding " প্রশাসনিক " (administerial) and "ব্যবস্থাপনামূলক " (managerial) post cannot be termed as worker and hence, is not legally entitled to enforce Chapter XV of the Act, 2006. 

 15. Instant writ petition has been placed before this Court at the instance of 7 (seven) petitioners basing their stand as "workers". Subsequently, 3(three) more persons were added as respondent Nos. 10-12 allowing the prayer of the petitioners who are also claiming as workers of the respondent Nos. 7 and 8 companies. Of those 7 (seven) writ petitioners, petitioner No.1 was appointed by the respondent No.8, Aggreko International Projects Ltd. (Bangladesh Branch Office) on 20-10-2011 in the post of Human Resource Manager, giving effect from 20-11-2011 (Annexure-C). Petitioner No.2 was appointed by the respondent No.8 on 14-5-2012 as Chief Accountant with effect from 14-6-2011 (Annexure-C1); petitioner No.3 was appointed by the respondent No.8 on 1-9-2011 in the post of Site Accountant with effect from 1-9-2011 (Annexure-C2); petitioner No.4 was also appointed by the respondent No.8 on 3-10-2011 as QHSE Co-ordinator with effect from 10-11-2011 (Annexure-C3). Petitioner No.5 was appointed by the respondent No.7, Aggreko international Power Projects Ltd. on 14-11-2013 as Mechanic giving effect from 15-11-2013; petitioner No.6 was appointed by the respondent No.7 on 14-11-2013 as Electrician with effect from 15-11-2013; and petitioner No.7 was appointed by the respondent No.7 on 14-11-2013 as Electrician with effect from 15-11-2013. 

 17. Thus, it is apparent from the above that petitioner Nos. 1-4 and added respondent No.10 were appointed in their respective posts prior to amendment of the word "worker" as defined in section 2(65) of the Act, 2006 which excludes certain categories of posts of the respective company from being called as worker i.e. managerial and administrative posts. 

 18. However, the terms, managerial, administrative and supervising officer have been defined in Rules 2(1) (cha) and 2(1)(ঞ) of the "বাংলাদেশ শ্রম বিধিমালা, ২০১৫"  (in short, Rules, 2015), which came into force on 15-9-2015 and accordingly, are quoted below for ready reference: 

 20. Rule 2(1) (ঞ) defines "প্রশাসনিক বা ব্যবস্থাপনামূলক কাজে দায়িত্বপ্রাপ্ত কোন ব্যক্তি” or, "person engaged in an administrative or managerial capacity", which is quoted below:— 

 22. In order to substantiate the argument that all the petitioners including the added respondent Nos.l0-12 are workers for enforcement of their right to workers" participation under the Act, 2006 Mr. Md. Helal Uddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners and Mr. Md. Anisul Hassan, the learned Advocate appearing for the added respondent Nos.10-12 conjointly submit referring to their respective appointment letters that none of the petitioners including the one who were appointed before amendment in 2013 were "মালিক বা ব্যবস্থাপনা কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক লিখিতভাবে ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত এমন কোন ব্যক্তি” to carry out the functions of a "supervising officer" or were involved in "administrative or managerial" activities because there was no "express written authority" issued by the respondent No.7 and 8 in this regard. It has also been argued that all the petitioners were mere workers and had only discharged their respective functions in the manner explained by their respective Line Manager. as mentioned in their employment contract. 

 23. Elaborating the said contention their further argument is that the petitioner No.1 was employed on 20-11-2011 as Human Resource (HR) Manager who was accountable to report to his Line Manager. He did not have any authority to appoint, terminate or remove employees or workers, determine wages and allowance etc. The whole recruitment procedure to hire workers of the company is that the HR Manager has to raise a request to fulfill the vacant position, then the request will have to be endorsed by the Area Operation Manager (AOM) followed by the final approval by the Asia LT, HR Director-APS and MD-APS respectively. Once recruited or appointment confirmed by the higher management authority as mentioned above, the contract of employment shall be issued by the company. In this regard, it has also been argued that as a general practice in all the companies around the world (including Bangladesh) the persons working in the human resource department are responsible for issuance of any kind of communication to sign documents on behalf of the company. Mere signing of documents/issuing of any communication do not mean that the person signing the document on behalf of the company is actually the 'hiring/firing' authority of an employee of the company. The HR department's employees like the petitioner No. 1 is merely to execute the orders/decisions of the company's management who does not have any authority to independently take any decision about whom to appoint or terminate, unless stated/ordered by the company's management. Therefore, only the management of the company has the authority to appoint or remove any employees determine salaries and allowance or benefits of the employees. Similarly, the petitioner Nos. 2-4 only followed the procedures and directions set by the higher management of the company in relation to the respective department; hence, the petitioner No. 1-4 do not come under the exception clause as stated in section 2(65) of Act. 2006. 

 24. In this connection referring to the ratio, as has been decided by the Appellate Division in the cases of Senior Manager MA. Dosta Textile Mills Ltd., Ranirhat, Feni and others vs Sudhansu Bikash Nath reported in 40 DLR (AD) 45 and Pioneer Garments Limited represented by its Managing Director vs Md. Abul Kellam Azad and another reported in 52 DLR (AD) 45, it has been contended that in those cases the categorical findings of the Appellate Division is that "mere designation" is not sufficient to indicate whether a person is a 'worker' or an 'employer', but it is the nature of the work, showing the extent of his authority which determines whether he is a worker or employer. Even if it is taken that he has supervisory function, still mere supervisory capacity will not bring him into the category of "employer". Moreover, as has been argued, salaries and other benefits of an employee does not/ cannot determine whether a person should be labelled as a "worker" or "non-worker". 

 25. Controverting the said assertions, Mr. Sharif Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.8 by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary-affidavit to the affidavit-in-opposition submits that the petitioners Nos. 1 to 4, who joined on different dates in 2011 and 2012, were not "workers" insofar as they were part of the management board of the respondent No.8 who managed by way of exercising managerial or administrative or supervisory functions of the respondent No.8 (Branch Office in Bangladesh). In support of the said contention he goes to argue that the petitioner No.1 was the Senior Human Resources Manager who had authority to recruit employees for the respondent No.8. He appointed petitioners Nos.5 to 7 to the employment of the respondent No.8 (Annexures 6, 7 and 8 respectively); petitioner No.2 was the Chief Accountant who was responsible for among others, annual budget and plans, and providing direction, coaching training to ensure a fully effective financial functions of the respondent No.8; petitioner No.3 was the Management Accountant who was responsible to manage, among others, budget of the respondent No.8; petitioner No.4 was the QHSE Manager who was responsible for ensuring compliance with the safety policies and procedure by all the employees of the respondent No.8. In this regard, he also submits that the annual gross salary including housing, medical and car and bonuses including festival and performance bonuses of the petitioner No.1 was Taka 46,92,035 for the year 2018-2019, the petitioner No.2 was Taka 21,17,789 for the year 2015-2016, the petitioner No.3 was Taka 16,07,764 for the year 2015-2016 and of the petitioner No.4 was Taka 20,88.464 for the year 2012-2013. 

 27. No doubt, mere designation is not sufficient to indicate whether a person is a `worker' or an 'employer' but it is the nature of the work showing extent of his authority which determines whether he is a worker or employer, as has been observed by our apex Court in Senior Mange,: MA. Dosta Textile Mills Ltd. Ranirhat, Feni and others vs Sudhansu Bikaslr Nadi: 40 DLR (AD) 45. In the given context onus lies squarely upon the petitioners and the added respondent No.10 to prove that the post of Human Resource Manager, Chief Accountant/Site Accountant of COHSE Co-ordinator being held by them before amendment, are not in the nature of administrative/ managerial/supervising capacity in view of the description of job as has been prescribed against the respective posts vide Annexures-17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23 and 24 respectively of the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No.8 and thus, involving question of facts to be proved by evidence. 

 28. In Pioneer Garments Ltd. represented by its Managing Director vs Md. Abul Kalam Azad reported in 52 DLR (AD) 45 para 4 the Appellate Division while giving findings on the arguments that the petitioner though was appointed as the Production Manager but was not given any managerial or supervisory responsibilities and that his duty was confined to physical and manual kind of work has categorically observed, inter-alia, that "In writ jurisdiction it cannot enter into the factual aspect of the case i.e. whether respondent No.1 is a Production Manager only in name or whether he is actually working in a managerial capacity. This fact is to be determined by the Labour Court and not by the High Court Division". Further, it has been observed that "whether the post in question is the post of an officer or a worker or workman is purely a question of fact which ought to have been agitated before the Labour Court".
